newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 10.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- The government's plan to increase spending by almost four percent ahead of inflation next year has provoked opposition claims that public expenditure is running out of control.
- Irish prime minister John Bruton made an impassioned appeal for a new IRA ceasefire on Monday night after failing to secure British agreement on a fixed date for Sinn Fein's entry into talks.

- The names of politicians or public servants mentioned in the Price Waterhouse report as having received contributions from Ben Dunne or Dunnes Stores are not now expected to be published for several weeks.
- Irish opposition leader Bertie Ahern said on Monday that the Anglo-Irish summit did little or nothing to move the peace process forward on Northern Ireland.

- Growth in world trade has slowed more than expected this year because of sluggish demand in the West for consumer goods, according to the World Trade Organisation's annual report published on Monday.
- The Irish government has thrown down the gauntlet to its huge public sector workforce by ruling out any new pay increases in the spending estimates for next year.
- A nurse has become the first person known to get the HIV virus from a blood transfusion -- and up to 15 others may have been infected in the same way, the southeast Health Board said.
- Irish prime minister John Bruton and British premier John Major failed to resolve their differences over the timing and conditions of Sinn Fein's entry into inter-party talks.
- The BSE crisis would result in extra spending next year on beef intervention and a more extensive computerised tracing system for cattle, Agriculture Minister Ivan Yates said.
- Government pay negotiators on Monday refused to concede to state workers the 9.25 percent pay increase agreed for the private sector.
